This was a well-specified math problem with a single correct answer, so capability is what matters most here. Dunlin-235B leads across the board on the relevant benchmarks — notably MMLU-Pro (80.9 vs 75.9) and GPQA Diamond (64.8 vs 56.2) — which signal stronger quantitative reasoning. The Extraction & Retrieval eval gap (84.8 vs 79.2) also exceeds the variance threshold, favoring Dunlin.

The task-preference notes didn't conflict with that: the query is warm in tone and not harm-adjacent, so none of Dunlin's aversions are triggered. And while Avocet self-reports a preference for well-specified tasks like this one, the documentation is explicit that those preferences are dissociated from actual output quality — so they don't override the capability advantage.

Net result: Dunlin is the stronger choice on the dimensions that actually affect answer quality.
